title: Structuring High-Stakes Data Narratives
description: Master the craft of transforming complex datasets into compelling executive narratives that drive strategic decisions.

interactions.prompt: Shopify's Q3 report shows: GMV up 22%, merchant count up 31%, but revenue per merchant down 14% YoY. ARPU declined in 5 of 6 regions. Which signal anchors the strongest data story for the board?

options.text: GMV growth proves platform health and market dominance
Merchant growth is diluting revenue quality at scale
Regional ARPU decline suggests pricing model weakness
Revenue per merchant drop is a temporary onboarding lag

interactions.prompt: A DoorDash data team presents: delivery time down 8%, customer NPS up 12 points, but dasher churn rose 23% and dasher satisfaction fell 19 points. The CFO asks for the real story. What's the critical narrative tension?

options.text: Customer gains are being subsidized by unsustainable labor pressure
Operational efficiency is improving across all customer-facing metrics
Dasher churn is normal seasonal variance not worth highlighting
NPS gains will self-correct dasher retention over time

chartData.title: Key Performance Metrics: Customer vs Dasher Impact

interactions.prompt: You're presenting Stripe's fraud detection results to non-technical regulators. Your model reduced false positives by 40% but uses a complex ensemble method. You have 10 minutes. How do you frame it?

options.text: Lead with the model architecture to establish credibility first
Anchor on customer harm prevented, use one simplified analogy for method
Present full statistical validation then translate to business outcomes
Skip methodology entirely and only discuss dollar impact

interactions.prompt: In advanced data storytelling, the 'So What → Now What' bridge fails when the analyst presents a statistically significant finding without connecting it to a ____ that the audience has authority to act on.

options.text: Decision or resource allocation
Visualization or dashboard
Confidence interval
Historical benchmark

interactions.prompt: You're structuring a data narrative for Airbnb's CEO about declining host acquisition in Europe. Rank these narrative elements from first to last in your presentation.

options.text: Detailed cohort analysis of host churn by European market segment
Strategic context: Europe host growth vs. global targets and competitive threat
Three prioritized recommendations with projected ROI and resource needs
Root cause synthesis: pricing, regulation, and onboarding friction ranked by impact

interactions.prompt: Your A/B test at Netflix shows a new recommendation algorithm lifts engagement 6% overall but decreases engagement 11% among the top-spending 8% of subscribers. The VP of Product wants one clear recommendation. What do you present?

options.text: Recommend full rollout since 92% of users benefit significantly
Recommend rollout with a carve-out preserving the old algorithm for top spenders
Recommend killing the experiment until the algorithm improves for all segments
Present both sides equally and let the VP decide without recommendation

interactions.prompt: A skeptical CFO at Peloton has rejected your last two data presentations. Rank these narrative repair strategies from most to least effective for rebuilding credibility.

options.text: Pre-align on her top three questions and structure the narrative around them
Add more charts and granular data to demonstrate analytical rigor
Lead with the limitations and uncertainty ranges before presenting conclusions
Open with a financial impact number she hasn't seen, tied to her OKRs

interactions.prompt: Midway through your presentation, the CEO reveals Uber is in acquisition talks for a last-mile logistics startup - making your organic growth narrative obsolete. With 5 minutes left, how do you pivot your data story?

options.text: Finish the original narrative since the data is still valid
Reframe your data as a due diligence baseline for evaluating the acquisition target
Abandon the presentation and ask to reschedule entirely
Pivot to showing only the competitive threat data as justification for acquiring

interactions.priorContext: You were presenting Uber's organic last-mile delivery growth strategy with 18 months of cohort data and a $200M investment recommendation. The CEO just disclosed confidential acquisition talks that could replace the entire organic approach.
